transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep forgetting basic adult responsibilities, and it’s starting to have real consequences. Like I’ll forget to pay bills, or I won’t return emails for interviews, or I’ll miss appointments. Even errands I fully mean to do just don’t get done. It’s been costing me opportunities, and I feel like I can’t keep up.
Have you experienced this kind of forgetfulness and trouble following through on tasks since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

It’s definitely been around since I was a kid. In elementary school, my teachers would say I was bright, but I was always losing worksheets or not turning things in because I couldn’t find them. I’d rush through directions, talk out of turn, and my desk was usually such a mess that I couldn’t find assignments. So it doesn’t feel like something that just started recently.
Right now, do you notice yourself feeling restless, needing to move around, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or blurting things out—on a regular basis?

Yes, pretty regularly. If I have to sit through something like an interview, a meeting, or even a movie, I get this pressure in my body like I need to move. I’ll shift around a lot or need to do something with my hands, and if I can’t, it feels like I’m going to crawl out of my skin.

Do these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and follow-through show up in more than one area of your life—for example, both at work and at home, or in your relationships—not just in one specific setting?

Yes, it’s definitely more than one area. Since I got fired, I’ve missed follow-up emails for interviews, and that’s made it harder to get back to work. I also had to step back from a volunteer project I really cared about because I couldn’t keep up reliably. So it feels like it’s affecting the basic steps of moving my life forward, not just one setting.

When you feel that restless, need-to-move sensation, is it usually accompanied by persistent worry or fear about specific things, or does it happen even when you're not particularly anxious about anything?

It happens even when I’m not especially worried about anything. Like, I can be in a meeting or watching a movie and not feel scared or anxious, but I still get that pressure in my body where I need to move, shift around, or do something with my hands. If I can’t, it feels like I’m going to crawl out of my skin.

latest_inference.note: Confirmed restlessness/hyperactivity occurs independent of anxiety or worry, ruling out generalized anxiety disorder as an explanation. Combined with childhood onset, cross-setting impairment, and both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms, this supports ADHD combined presentation as the sole remaining diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong (since elementary school) pattern of both inattentive symptoms (losing worksheets, forgetting to turn in assignments, forgetting bills/appointments, poor follow-through, disorganization) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (motor restlessness, need to move, talking out of turn, inability to sit still). Symptoms are present across multiple settings (work, home, volunteer activities) and have caused significant functional impairment (job loss, missed interviews, inability to sustain volunteer commitment). The restlessness is not better explained by anxiety, as it occurs independent of worry or fear. Combined presence of both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptom clusters since childhood, with cross-situational impairment, supports ADHD, Combined Type (F90.2) rather than predominantly inattentive (F90.0) or predominantly hyperactive-impulsive (F90.1) subtypes.
